title: Sections of the pullback of a quasi-coherent module over an affine open
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal G$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $f^*\mathcal G$ its pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], with unit $\eta_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to f_*f^*\mathcal G$ of the adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$; for an open $W\subseteq Y$ and $s\in\mathcal G(W)$ write $f^*s=\eta_{\mathcal G}(s)\in(f^*\mathcal G)(f^{-1}W)$. Let $V\subseteq Y$ and $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ be affine opens, $A=\mathcal O_Y(V)$, $B=\mathcal O_X(U)$, and $\rho:A\to B$, $\rho(a)=f^\sharp_V(a)|_U$, the ring map induced by $f$ (so $B$ is an $A$-algebra and $\mathcal G(V)\otimes_AB$ a $B$-module through the second factor). Then the map
$$c_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G(V)\otimes_AB\longrightarrow(f^*\mathcal G)(U),\qquad s\otimes b\longmapsto b\cdot(f^*s)|_U,$$
is a well-defined isomorphism of $B$-modules, and it is natural in $\mathcal G$: for every $\mathcal O_Y$-linear $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ between quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, $(f^*u)_U\circ c_{\mathcal G}=c_{\mathcal G'}\circ(u_V\otimes1_B)$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback) part (1): psi^* M~ = (S (x)_R M)~ for a morphism of affine schemes Spec S -> Spec R, functorially in M; combined with Lemma 01IA (lemma-quasi-coherent-affine: G|_V = G(V)~ on an affine V), Lemma 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves: global sections of N~ are N) and the compatibility of f^* with restriction to opens (Sheaves, Lemma 00A0, lemma-j-pullback; Modules, Lemma 01AJ, lemma-exactness-pushforward-pullback, f^* as a left adjoint); this is the affine description used in the proof of Modules, Lemma 01BG (lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent, modules.tex). Stacks states no separate lemma for an affine open U of X lying over an affine open V of Y (statement assembled by the agent).

proof.text: Restrict the chosen tensor-pullback adjunction unit from f^{-1}V to U. It is A-linear by linearity of the unit and the restriction scalar formula, with scalar map f.appLE. Extend (s,b) mapping to b times this restricted unit through TensorProduct.lift. Tensor induction proves B-linearity on the second factor.
Apply the affine pure-tensor-map bijectivity theorem to the constructed map.

Naturality of the chosen adjunction unit and compatibility of the pulled-back morphism with restrictions prove naturality on pure tensors. Its B-linearity moves b outside. Additivity and tensor induction handle every tensor.
